title: Shield a culture dish with its lid while adding medium
instruction: Add one pipetteful of fresh medium from the reservoir to the culture dish, holding the dish's lid over it as a shield with the opening toward the back wall, then put the lid back on, stand the pipette in its holder and let go.
context: Why: dishes of cells are fed inside a Class II biological safety cabinet, and the open dish is where contamination gets in. CDC/NIH BMBL (Appendix A) tells workers to hold Petri dish and culture plate lids above the open sterile surface so the downflow does not impact it directly; the Galloway Lab (MIT) culture protocol: lift the lid with one hand while pipetting with the other, the lid covering as much as possible, just enough opening, the opening facing the back wall, and add liquid against the side wall, not onto the cells. The natural move, taking the lid off and setting it beside the dish, leaves the dish open for the whole transfer. The knack: one hand lifts the lid clear of the rim and tilts it up at its back edge, low edge close to the rim, while the other brings the pipette down through the back gap and squeezes at the side wall; then the lid goes straight back. Done by: technicians and students in every cell-culture lab, several times a week per dish.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the work surface. Cabinet: the two-arm robot works inside a Thermo Scientific 1300 Series Class II Type A2 biological safety cabinet, 4-foot, interior 1199 x 780 x 630 mm (W x H x D, maker's brochure), stainless steel; arm bases 15 cm behind the 10 cm front air grille, the sash behind them at its 10 in (254 mm) working height, the back wall at x 48.0 cm with a 5 cm rear exhaust grille, the HEPA diffuser 78 cm up. An arm link past a wall, the ceiling or the sash plane, or an object within 4 in of the front grille or on the rear grille, scores 0. Repeated trials may use a full-size plywood mock of this interior (acrylic sash, tape-band grilles). Dish: a Corning 430166 60 mm tissue-culture dish (maker: 15 mm tall with its lid, growth floor 52.1 mm across, 4.2-6.3 mL of medium), polystyrene, dry; base 54.5 mm across with 1.2 mm walls, rim 14 mm up, 9 g; lid 60 mm across, 1 mm top with an 8 mm skirt, 6 g (base, lid and masses estimated); free, lid seated, centred at x 25.0 cm, y -1.0 cm. The floor is the cell layer. Medium: a Corning 4870 sterile 50 mL reagent reservoir (145 x 70 x 28 mm, white polystyrene, 15 g), long side along x, free, centred at x 20.0 cm, y -15.0 cm, holding 40 mL of pink-dyed water. Pipette: a sterile graduated transfer pipette, 5 mL large bulb (CellPro class), drawing 5.0 mL per full squeeze: bulb 20 x 28 x 30 mm across its squeeze faces, which give 9 mm each, stem 6 mm across and 120 mm long, 15 cm overall, 38 g, empty, standing tip-down in a holder, its squeeze faces toward bearing 30 deg. Holder: a 3D-printed block with a 24 mm square well 65 mm deep, fixed, at x 21.0 cm, y -23.5 cm. Friction 0.5 (set). Both arms start in their ready pose. One fixed layout, zero object jitter. Nothing else is on the work surface.
scoring: Watched every step, in the dish's frame. The lid is off when any point of its skirt's bottom edge is more than 5 mm above its seated height. While off it must be a shield: its centre within 25 mm (horizontal) of the dish axis, its lowest rim point at most 20 mm above the dish rim, tilted at most 45 deg, and, once tilted more than 10 deg, its highest point within 60 deg of the direction of the back wall from its centre. 0 if, at any time: the shield rule breaks; the pipette touches the lid, the dish's rim, outside or floor (contact, 0.02 mm; the inner side wall may be touched); medium is squeezed out over no vessel; the dish slides more than 5 mm; the lid or pipette falls more than 20 mm within 0.25 s; or a cabinet rule breaks. Also 0 unless the dish ends with 5.0 mL (+-0.3) and every squeeze into it was made with the tip below the rim and within 8 mm of the side wall. 0.5: that, with the lid not seated at the end or the dish open more than 30 s in all. 0.75: also the lid seated (its whole rim within 2 mm of seated height, centre within 3 mm) after at most 30 s open, but the pipette not standing in its holder (tip inside the well, tilted at most 20 deg) or a gripper within 20 mm of lid or pipette, or something still moving. 1.0: all of that, both grippers clear and nothing moving more than 1 mm for 1 s. Real trial: a phone overhead (lid centre and bearing against marks on the work surface; the tip against a ring drawn 8 mm inside the wall), a phone at bench level with a 1 mm grid card behind the dish (heights, tilt), video timestamps for the open time; a frame of the tip on the lid, rim or floor is a touch; the dish weighed on a 0.01 g balance before and after (5.0 g +-0.3).
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted two-arm demo takes about 37 s
reset_notes: A fresh dish and lid each trial (or dry them), weighed empty; lid seated on the base at its mark. Top the reservoir up to 40 mL. A fresh pipette, empty, standing in the holder with its squeeze faces as stated. Grid card and floor ring in place.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at catalogue size; dish and lid 12-sided. No liquid: a ledger moves it. A full squeeze empties the pipette into the vessel its tip is in (or over the dish within 10 mm of the rim); a release under the surface draws what lies above the tip, up to 5 mL. Bulb sides on 350 N/m springs, 9 mm travel. Reservoir's U-bottom taken flat. A pink tint shows the dish's volume. Friction 0.5, static = dynamic.
